leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 configurations are a single-part B034 prize on GLP-1 physiology and incretin-based therapies, and all six name Drucker and Holst. They differ on the third laureate and the citation. El Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius name Mojsov for identification and synthesis of the active peptide, with citations framed around physiology and the active form. Svenningsson names Knudsen instead, with a citation that explicitly covers long-acting therapies. No member proposes four names, and no member proposes Habener. Shared: B034 is first, the case rests on the chain of evidence rather than on opening-round unanimity, and maturity is not in doubt. Not shared: whether the prize is framed as discovery physiology or as discovery plus drug development.

areas_of_agreement: All six members prefer B034 as the single-achievement prize in round 1, and each says the case rests on the evidence chain (proglucagon processing, the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, incretin physiology and receptor biology, long-acting agonists) and not on opening-round unanimity.
All six name Drucker and Holst in their preferred configuration.

All six describe the work as mature and independently confirmed, citing large randomized outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal disease; no member raises a timing objection to B034.
All six list B003 and B040 as their alternatives, in that order, and none lists another ballot.
All six state that attribution is the main weakness of B034, and each says the supplied credit list cannot fully settle it.
Each of the six records that no specific conflict applies to any shortlisted candidate.
scientific_disputes: No member disputes the scientific validity of B034. The open scientific question is framing: whether the prize honours the discovery of GLP-1 physiology and its active form, or the translation into durable drugs. Members say this framing decides between Mojsov and Knudsen as third laureate.

El Manira, Linnarsson and Sandberg describe a discovery-side prize as the more defensible reading of the tradition. Svenningsson says that if the committee wants a discovery-only framing his configuration is the less conservative choice, and he accepts that naming Knudsen honours industrial development, which some members will not regard as discovery.

Perlmann and Wahren-Herlenius describe B003 (unfolded protein response) as a basic discovery with a clean attribution but only a partial disease-translation record, so its medical case is weaker than B034's.

El Manira says he would not combine B003 with B034, because a two-part prize would cut the GLP-1 credit to two names. Svenningsson raises a reduced GLP-1 part paired with UPR or CAR-T as a question. Sandberg does not endorse optogenetics (B026) as a preferred prize, calling it a tool rather than a disease-mechanism discovery. Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius each raise the CAR-T (B040) question as unresolved.
attribution_disputes: Priority for identifying the bioactive GLP-1 peptide is contested between Mojsov and Habener's group. All six members flag this, and Habener is not among the credited names on the shortlist. Sandberg, Wahren-Herlenius and Linnarsson say the supplied evidence does not let them settle priority independently.

The third-laureate choice splits five to one in round 1: Mojsov (El Manira, Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg, Wahren-Herlenius) against Knudsen (Svenningsson). El Manira says that if priority review shows Mojsov's claim cannot be sustained, he would prefer to substitute Knudsen rather than move to another candidate, and that he would not do so on public controversy alone.

Any three-name cut omits either a discoverer or the drug developer. Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius each note that omitting Knudsen leaves out the long-acting analogues that reached patients, while Svenningsson notes that his configuration leaves out Mojsov's contested identification claim.

For B040, Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg and Wahren-Herlenius raise the omission of Eshhar and other early chimeric-receptor originators from the credited names (June, Sadelain, Rosenberg), and Wahren-Herlenius also raises the Rosenberg attribution. For B026, the six-name credit list means no member sees a defensible three-person cut.
maturity_disputes: No maturity dispute is recorded for B034. Members describe it as confirmed by several independent outcome trials, and Wahren-Herlenius calls it arguably overdue.

B003 is described as a very mature basic discovery whose human therapeutic validation is thin, and Perlmann notes that the integrated stress response and the PERK and ATF6 branches may be hard to separate from the core UPR story.
El Manira lists as unresolved whether long-term safety questions for incretin therapy would change the maturity assessment. No other member raises this.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: No member declares a conflict or recusal need for any shortlisted candidate.

Svenningsson discloses co-authorship with Perlmann (dopamine neurons, Nurr1) and a postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard, neither a shortlisted candidate. Perlmann discloses past work with Svenningsson and El Manira and a Salk-period collaboration with Ronald Evans, not credited on the shortlist. El Manira discloses collaborations with Grillner and Ernfors and a 2009 paper with Perlmann, none credited on the shortlist. Linnarsson discloses spatial-transcriptomics co-authorship and a KI affiliation. Sandberg discloses co-authorship with Linnarsson and with Frisen (outside the committee) and KI training. Wahren-Herlenius discloses co-authors Kuchroo and Sonesson and a Bergen affiliation, and notes that autoimmunity is a field adjacent to B029 and B040 but not a personal tie.
questions_for_round2: Should the B034 citation be framed around the physiology of GLP-1 and its active form, or around physiology plus the development of long-acting therapies, and should that framing be settled before the third name is chosen?

Is Mojsov's identification of the active GLP-1 peptide sufficiently documented, given Habener's group's claim, to be credited as the third laureate, and what primary-record evidence would the committee need to decide?
If Mojsov's priority cannot be sustained, should Knudsen replace her within B034, or should the committee move to a different candidate?
Can the committee defend omitting Habener, and omitting either Knudsen or Mojsov, in a three-name B034 citation, and what wording would state that limit?
If B034 does not gain a four-vote majority on a specific three-name configuration, is B003 or B040 the preferred second choice, and why?
Does a two-part prize pairing a reduced B034 with B003 or B040 improve on a single-part B034 prize, given that a two-part design would cut the GLP-1 credit to two names?
For B040, can the omission of Eshhar and other early chimeric-receptor originators from the credited names be resolved, and does it make a June, Sadelain and Rosenberg prize fair?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows complete agreement on B034 as the preferred prize and on Drucker and Holst, with a five-to-one split on the third name and a shared view that framing, not merit or maturity, decides that choice. Alternatives are identical across members (B003 then B040), so round 1 does not discriminate between them. Four votes on a specific configuration is not yet reached, because the six-member majority threshold applies to an exact set of laureates and citation: five configurations name Mojsov and one names Knudsen. Round 2 needs to resolve the framing and priority questions, not reopen the case for B034.
